clue.text: Horse has quickly to go over the other way

indicators.note: the other way tells us to read the summarising word from its end back to its start

parts.note: to recap is to go over something quickly, summarising it

explanation.surface: A racehorse must hurry back round the course in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way' turns RECAP round to give the horse; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse trained to race at a pace, a two-legs-together trotting gait, typically in harness racing.

clue.text: As job, I drive around carriage

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: around shows the word for drive goes round the single letter

parts.note: to chase is to drive away or pursue

explanation.surface: A coachman says driving round the carriage is his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts CHASE round I to make CHAISE; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-chaise was a hired horse-drawn carriage for travelling by stages.

clue.text: Officer's brief depression

definitions.meaning: a short form of the rank Colonel
a dip or pass between two mountain peaks

explanation.definitionFit: Col is the abbreviated rank of a colonel and also a low pass in a mountain ridge.

clue.text: Ready to include European Community in procedure

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so the word for ready takes the two letters inside

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Brussels is ready to bring the EU into its formal process.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions, a method or procedure for achieving something.

clue.text: Manoeuvre ship clear, as cannonballs appear

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move around skilfully, so the letters of the next two words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Steering a vessel out of the way while round shot comes flying in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvre' rearranges SHIPCLEAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannonballs are round balls of iron, so they look ball-shaped.

clue.text: Calculator making slip with formula

parts.note: to slide is to slip
a rule is a principle or formula

explanation.surface: A pocket computer made by blundering with an equation.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide rule is a sliding scale device engineers used for doing multiplication before electronic calculators.

clue.text: One of a line of so-called kings, such as James

definitions.text: One of a line of so-called kings
definitions.meaning: eight English kings bore this name
the first name of the novelist James, author of The Turn of the Screw

explanation.definitionFit: England had eight kings of that name, and Henry James was the American-born novelist.

clue.text: Missile activity involving old engine on line

parts.note: Stephenson's Rocket was a famous early steam locomotive
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Ballistic tests that use a vintage locomotive on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' and 'on' are links; ROCKET here is the historic railway engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science and practice of building and launching rockets, i.e. missiles.

clue.text: Mathematical study of disorganisation on the Circle Line?

parts.note: chaos is complete disorder
taken as written
the letter O is circle-shaped
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A study of disorder on the London Underground's Circle line, famous for delays.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground line; here it splits into the O (circle) and RY (railway line); 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos theory is a branch of mathematics studying systems highly sensitive to initial conditions.

clue.text: Physician left small instrument here

parts.note: uke is short for ukulele, a small guitar

explanation.surface: A doctor forgot his little ukulele here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is a link; the Physician is St Luke, called 'the beloved physician' in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Luke the Evangelist is described in the Bible as a physician, a doctor.

clue.text: There's still a choice to be made if leader goes

definitions.text: There's still a choice to be made if leader goes

parts.words: There's still a choice to be made if leader goes
parts.note: the answer means a choice; take away its first letter and what remains is a vote, still a choice to be made

explanation.surface: Even if the party leader steps down, voters still have options.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a choice or pick; lose the leading S and an election remains, another kind of choosing.

clue.text: It's not like cheese that's put on board

definitions.text: It's not like cheese that's put on board

parts.words: It's not like cheese that's put on board
parts.note: plays on the phrase 'like ... and cheese' for two utterly different things, and on writing on a blackboard

explanation.surface: Something unlike a cheese course that gets served up on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a cheeseboard, but it is a teacher's blackboard; the British idiom 'as different as chalk and cheese' means utterly unlike.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalk is the white stick used for writing on a blackboard, and the stock opposite of cheese in the British idiom.

clue.text: Top sportsmen see sights, one of them in Paris

parts.note: champs is short for champions, the top sportsmen
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is one
to sight something is to see it, so sights gives sees

explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is a noun: a bishop's see, here ELY, a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Champs-Élysées is the great avenue of Paris, one of the city's famous sights.

clue.text: One part of bridge is twitching, resisting all control

parts.note: an means one
an arch supports a bridge
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: One span of the bridge is shaking out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitching' gives TIC, a nervous spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchistic means rejecting all government and authority, refusing any form of order.

clue.text: Play first match when game's in most danger

definitions.meaning: to stage the opening fixture of a sporting season
the period when hunting animals for sport is allowed

explanation.definitionFit: To open the season is to play its first fixture; an open season is when hunting quarry is legal.

clue.text: A style found abroad

parts.note: a way of doing something is a style or manner

explanation.surface: A fashion first spotted in foreign countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being out of the country, elsewhere from home.

clue.text: Occupation resulting in work or play?

definitions.text: Occupation resulting in work or play?

parts.words: Occupation resulting in work or play?
parts.note: a job whose output is a written work, such as a novel, or a stage play

explanation.surface: Asking which line of employment yields either labour or leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work or play' reads as labour versus leisure, but a work is a book and a play is a drama: both are what writers produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorship is the profession of writing, whose products are literary works and plays.

clue.text: In which falls mean slipped discs?

definitions.text: In which falls mean slipped discs?

parts.words: In which falls mean slipped discs?
parts.note: a falling position in a ranking of records means those records have slipped

explanation.surface: Medical: where taking a tumble leads to spinal injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipped discs' suggests the back injury, but the discs are records sliding down the pop chart.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is a ranked chart of the best-selling records.

clue.text: Cost of carrying horse inside city state

parts.note: cartage is the charge for carrying goods by cart
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: Paying to have a horse transported into the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was an ancient North African city state, Rome's great rival.

clue.text: Matrimony, possibly, requires ring here in California

parts.note: marriage is one of the Christian sacraments, so matrimony is an example of one
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wedding demands a ring in this American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the wedding ring of the surface, but gives only the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California, a place in that state.

clue.text: Part of speech with negative components

parts.note: no is a negative word
un- is a negative prefix, as in unhappy

explanation.surface: A grammar term made up of refusals.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is built from two negatives, the word NO and the prefix UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is a word class, one of the parts of speech, naming a thing, person or place.

clue.text: One of a pair of composers said to be merry

definitions.text: One of a pair of composers
definitions.meaning: the German composer often paired with Liszt in the phrase
'... and Liszt' is British rhyming slang for pissed, drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a composer; British rhyming slang 'Brahms and Liszt' means drunk, i.e. merry.

clue.text: Feature of poem that could be eternal?

definitions.text: Feature of poem that could be eternal?

parts.words: Feature of poem that could be eternal?
parts.note: a rhyme placed inside a line rather than at its end; the word eternal itself has a rhyming part internal to it

explanation.surface: Wondering which element of verse might last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eternal' suggests timelessness, but it is offered as an example: the word rhymes with the first half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal rhyme is rhyme between words within a single line of verse, a poetic device.

clue.text: Three characters from 6 bring a case back

indicators.note: three characters taken from the answer at 6 down leave five letters

parts.note: the answer to 6 down

explanation.surface: Removing three letters from a missile word to reopen a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is the cross-reference to 6 down; taking out OCK leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To retry a case is to hear it again in court, bringing it back before a judge.

clue.text: Greek school of philosophy, from Pythagoras to Aristotle

indicators.note: from signals the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A Greek school of thought spanning everyone from Pythagoras to Aristotle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters out of PythagoraS TO Aristotle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoa was the colonnade in Athens where Zeno taught, giving the Stoics their name.

clue.text: Fish — importing four at the start of term

definitions.meaning: a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish kept in aquariums

definitions.text: four at the start of term
definitions.meaning: the Greek prefix meaning four, found at the start of terms like tetrahedron

clue.text: Lessons producing pain in backward set

parts.note: taken as written, a set being a group
aching is a dull persistent pain

explanation.walkthrough: 'backward set' sounds like a slow class of pupils, but 'backward' turns the group word round to TES; 'producing' is only a link.

clue.text: Refusal to put spirit in water

definitions.meaning: a flat no, as in to say ... to something

explanation.definitionFit: Nix is slang for no or nothing, and also a water spirit of Germanic folklore.

clue.text: Model new teacher has to accept unknown pressure

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the shuffled letters take the two short pieces inside them
new signals the letters of the next word are made into something fresh

explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TEACHER into ARCHETE, and 'to accept' sets Y and P inside it; 'has' is a link.

clue.text: German performing with jazz instrument

parts.note: sax is short for saxophone, a staple of jazz
a performer is on, onstage

explanation.surface: A musician from Germany playing the saxophone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' means of a Germanic people, not a modern German.
